    Get field value copy (allocate new memory) Supports all data types including: - Basic types: BOOL, INT32, INT64, UINT32, UINT64, FLOAT, DOUBLE - String types: STRING, BINARY - Vector types: VECTOR_FP32, VECTOR_FP64, VECTOR_FP16, VECTOR_INT4, VECTOR_INT8, VECTOR_INT16, VECTOR_BINARY32, VECTOR_BINARY64 - Sparse vector types: SPARSE_VECTOR_FP32, SPARSE_VECTOR_FP16 - Array types: ARRAY_STRING, ARRAY_BINARY, ARRAY_BOOL, ARRAY_INT32, ARRAY_INT64, ARRAY_UINT32, ARRAY_UINT64, ARRAY_FLOAT, ARRAY_DOUBLE The returned value pointer must be manually freed using appropriate deallocation functions (zvec_free() for basic types and strings, zvec_free_uint8_array() for binary data).

      public static ZvecNative.zvec_string_t zvec_string_create_from_view(@Const ZvecNative.zvec_string_view_t view)
      Create string from string view Creates a new zvec_string_t by copying data from a zvec_string_view_t. The created string owns its memory and must be freed with zvec_free_string().
      Parameters:
      view - Pointer to source string view (must not be NULL)
      Returns:

    • zvec_bin_create

      public static ZvecNative.zvec_string_t zvec_bin_create(@Cast("const uint8_t*") org.bytedeco.javacpp.BytePointer data, @Cast("size_t") long length)
      Create binary-safe string from raw data Creates a new zvec_string_t from raw binary data that may contain null bytes. Unlike zvec_string_create(), this function takes explicit length parameter and doesn't rely on null-termination. The created string owns its memory and must be freed with zvec_free_string().
      Parameters:
      data - Raw binary data pointer (must not be NULL)
      length - Length of data in bytes
      Returns:
      zvec_string_t* New string instance on success, NULL on error Note: Caller is responsible for freeing the returned string Note: This function is suitable for binary data containing null bytes

      @Cast("zvec_io_backend_type_t") public static int zvec_get_io_backend_type()
      Get the current I/O backend type for DiskAnn disk reads. Linux selects the first usable backend in this order: io_uring, libaio, then synchronous pread. macOS ARM64 uses synchronous pread. Windows uses unbuffered overlapped I/O with a per-context completion port.
      Returns:
      zvec_io_backend_type_t The loaded backend type ZVEC_IO_BACKEND_TYPE_IO_URING, ZVEC_IO_BACKEND_TYPE_LIBAIO, ZVEC_IO_BACKEND_TYPE_PREAD, or ZVEC_IO_BACKEND_TYPE_WINDOWS_OVERLAPPED.

On Linux, the pread description also explains that io_uring and libaio were unavailable and provides guidance for enabling an asynchronous backend. Windows reports its overlapped-I/O backend.

    • zvec_index_params_set_fts_params

      @Cast("zvec_error_code_t") public static int zvec_index_params_set_fts_params(ZvecNative.zvec_index_params_t params, @Cast("const char*") org.bytedeco.javacpp.BytePointer tokenizer_name, @Const ZvecNative.zvec_string_array_t filters, @Cast("const char*") org.bytedeco.javacpp.BytePointer extra_params)
      Set FTS index specific parameters
      Parameters:
      params - Index parameters (must be FTS type)
      tokenizer_name - Tokenizer pipeline name (NULL keeps current value). Supported values are "standard", "ngram", "jieba", and "whitespace".
      filters - Token filter names (NULL keeps current value). Supported values are "lowercase", "ascii_folding", and "stemmer".
      extra_params - Additional tokenizer/filter parameters (NULL keeps current value). Must be empty or a JSON object string. Supported keys by tokenizer/filter: Tokenizers: standard: - "max_token_length" (positive integer). ngram: - "ngram_min" (positive integer, default 2). - "ngram_max" (positive integer, default 2). - "token_chars" (array of "letter", "digit", "whitespace", "punctuation", "symbol"; default [] keeps all valid UTF-8 characters). custom_token_chars is not supported. jieba: - "jieba_dict_dir" (optional external directory containing jieba.dict.utf8 and hmm_model.utf8; priority: field value > ZVEC_JIEBA_DICT_DIR > embedded defaults). - "user_dict_path" (user dictionary path; augments the selected dictionary, including the embedded default). - "cut_mode" ("search", "mix", "full", or "hmm"; default "search"). whitespace: - no extra_params. Filters: lowercase: - no extra_params. ascii_folding: - no extra_params. stemmer: - "stemmer_lang" (Snowball language/algorithm; default "english"), for example {"stemmer_lang":"porter"} for ES behaviour.
      Returns:
      ZVEC_OK on success, error code on failure

    • zvec_collection_create_iterator

      @Cast("zvec_error_code_t") public static int zvec_collection_create_iterator(ZvecNative.zvec_collection_t collection, @Const ZvecNative.zvec_iterator_options_t options, @Cast("zvec_doc_iterator_t**") org.bytedeco.javacpp.PointerPointer out_iter)
      Create a document iterator over the collection. Takes an isolated snapshot at call time. On a writable collection this seals the current writing segment (each call may produce a new small segment); read-only collections are scanned without any write. While any iterator is open, schema changes (create/drop index, add/alter/drop column) and destroy return an error, and optimize fails at its start; conversely this call fails while a maintenance operation (optimize, schema DDL or destroy) is running. Flush, writes and queries are not affected. zvec_collection_close() only releases the handle: the collection itself closes when the last handle is released, waiting for any open iterators first, so close every iterator (zvec_doc_iterator_close) before releasing the last collection handle.
      Parameters:
      collection - Collection handle
      options - Iterator options (may be NULL to use defaults)
      out_iter - [out] Returned iterator handle (release with zvec_doc_iterator_close)
      Returns:
      zvec_error_code_t Error code
